equation_request.abstract: A coinless, discrete-time quantum walk possesses a Hilbert space whose dimension is smaller compared to the widely-studied coined walk. Coined walks require the direct product of the site basis with the coin space, coinless walks operate purely in the site basis, which is clearly minimal. These coinless quantum walks have received considerable attention recently because they have evolution operators that can be obtained by a graphical method based on lattice tessellations and they have been shown to be as efficient as the best known coined walks when used as a quantum search algorithm. We argue that both formulations in their most general form are equivalent. In particular, we demonstrate how to transform the one-dimensional version of the coinless quantum walk into an equivalent extended coined version for a specific family of evolution operators. We present some of its basic, asymptotic features for the one-dimensional lattice with some examples of tessellations, and analyze the mixing time and limiting probability distributions on cycles.

specification.problem: Reconstruct a mathematical specification of a coinless (tessellation-based, 'staggered') discrete-time quantum walk on a one-dimensional lattice/cycle, acting purely on the site basis, including its two-tessellation evolution operator, the mapping to an equivalent coined walk, and the time-averaged limiting distribution and mixing time on cycles, as described in the abstract.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest useful construction: a coinless quantum walk on a cycle of N (even) sites with two tessellations, each tessellation consisting of N/2 two-site polygons (nearest-neighbour pairs), with the evolution operator U = U_1 U_0 where each U_j is a reflection about the span of its polygon states. Tiny explicit instance: N = 4 sites (2 qubits), polygon amplitudes with theta = theta' = pi/2 and zero phases, initial state localized at site 0, evolution for t steps followed by computational-basis measurement. Out of scope (not reconstructable from the abstract): the paper's specific family of evolution operators, the exact form of the 'extended coined' equivalent walk and the general-form equivalence argument, the asymptotic features derived for particular tessellations, and any numerical mixing-time results.

symbols.meaning: Number of sites on the cycle (assumed even so that two nearest-neighbour tessellations tile it)
Site label on the cycle, arithmetic modulo N
Computational-basis site state; x encoded as an n-bit integer on n = \log_2 N qubits (big-endian)
Polygon states of tessellation 0 (pairs {2k,2k+1}) and tessellation 1 (pairs {2k+1,2k+2 mod N})
Amplitude and phase parameters of the polygon states (assumed family)
Reflections associated with tessellations 0 and 1, and the one-step coinless evolution operator
Probability of finding the walker at site x after t steps
Time-averaged distribution up to time T, and its limiting (T to infinity) distribution
Orthogonal projector onto the eigenspace of U with eigenvalue \lambda
Mixing time to accuracy \varepsilon in total variation (L1) distance
Coin value in the equivalent coined picture (parity of site index)

equations.label: Coinless Hilbert space (site basis only)
equations.description: The coinless walk acts on the N-dimensional site space without any tensor-product coin factor, in contrast to the coined space \mathcal{H}_N \otimes \mathbb{C}^2.
equations.abstract_quote: coinless walks operate purely in the site basis, which is clearly minimal
equations.justification: Directly stated in the abstract; the dimension count follows from the site basis having N elements.
assumptions: Cycle of N sites with periodic boundary conditions (abstract mentions cycles).

equations.label: Polygon states of the two nearest-neighbour tessellations
equations.description: Each tessellation covers the cycle by disjoint two-site polygons; one unit vector with support on each polygon defines the tessellation's subspace. Site arithmetic is modulo N.
equations.justification: The abstract says the evolution operators come from lattice tessellations in 1D but does not give the polygon states; this is the simplest one-parameter-per-tessellation family consistent with that description. The paper's 'specific family of evolution operators' may differ.
assumptions: Two tessellations of two-site polygons (minimal 1D tessellation).
Uniform parameters (theta,phi) and (theta',phi') across all polygons of a tessellation (translation invariance).

equations.label: Coinless (staggered) evolution operator from the tessellations
equations.latex: U_0 = 2\sum_{k=0}^{N/2-1}|\alpha_k\rangle\langle\alpha_k| - I,\qquad U_1 = 2\sum_{k=0}^{N/2-1}|\beta_k\rangle\langle\beta_k| - I,\qquad U = U_1 U_0
equations.description: Each tessellation yields a unitary, Hermitian reflection (U_j^2 = I) about the span of its polygon states; one step of the walk is the product of the two reflections. Each U_j is block-diagonal in its own polygon decomposition, so it is implementable as parallel 2x2 unitaries.
equations.justification: This is the established tessellation (staggered) construction of coinless walks recalled from the literature; the abstract only names the graphical tessellation method without writing the operator.
assumptions: The paper's operators are of the reflection form 2P-I; generalizations (e.g. e^{i\theta P}) are not covered.

equations.label: Time evolution and site probability distribution
equations.description: Exact unitary evolution for t discrete steps; the measured quantity is the computational-basis probability distribution over sites.
equations.justification: Standard definition of a discrete-time quantum walk's state and position distribution; the localized initial state is a choice for the tiny instance.

equations.label: Time-averaged and limiting probability distribution on the cycle
equations.description: Because p_t(x) does not converge for a unitary walk, the limiting distribution is defined via Cesaro time averaging; the closed form sums over distinct eigenvalues of U with eigenspace projectors \Pi_\lambda, cross terms between distinct eigenvalues averaging to zero.
equations.justification: Standard result for limiting distributions of unitary quantum walks (Aharonov-Ambainis-Kempe-Vazirani style); the abstract states these are analyzed on cycles but gives no formulas.
assumptions: Limit is taken over integer times; eigenvalue degeneracies are handled by projectors onto full eigenspaces.

equations.label: Mixing time in total variation distance
equations.description: Time after which the time-averaged distribution stays within \varepsilon of its limiting distribution; defined relative to the Cesaro average, not the instantaneous distribution.
equations.justification: Standard definition of quantum mixing time; the abstract mentions analysing mixing time on cycles without supplying a formula or result.
assumptions: Total-variation (half L1) norm is used; other norms would change constants.

equations.label: Relabeling that maps the 1D coinless walk to a coined walk on N/2 cells
equations.latex: |2k + c\rangle \;\longleftrightarrow\; |k\rangle\otimes|c\rangle,\quad k\in\mathbb{Z}_{N/2},\;c\in\{0,1\},\qquad U_0 \mapsto I_{N/2}\otimes C_0,\quad C_0 = 2|\alpha\rangle\langle\alpha| - I_2
equations.description: Grouping each tessellation-0 polygon into a cell with a two-dimensional internal (coin) index makes U_0 a site-independent local coin operation C_0 (with |\alpha\rangle = \cos(\theta/2)|0\rangle + e^{i\phi}\sin(\theta/2)|1\rangle); U_1 couples neighbouring cells and plays the role of a (coin-dependent) shift combined with a second coin, giving an 'extended' coined walk. Dimensions agree exactly: N = (N/2)\times 2.
equations.abstract_quote: we demonstrate how to transform the one-dimensional version of the coinless quantum walk into an equivalent extended coined version for a specific family of evolution operators
equations.justification: The abstract claims such a transformation exists; the parity-based relabeling is the natural isometry under which the block structure of eq_3 becomes a coin operation. The precise decomposition of U_1 into shift and coin operations used by the paper is not given and is not reconstructed here.
assumptions: Cell size 2 (two-site polygons) so that the coin is two-dimensional.
The paper's 'extended coined' form is assumed to be reachable by a basis relabeling; details of its shift/coin factorization are not established.

registers.name: site
registers.size: n = \log_2 N qubits (instance: 2 qubits for N = 4)
registers.role: Encodes the walker's position x \in \mathbb{Z}_N as an n-bit big-endian integer; this is the entire Hilbert space (no coin register).

specification.initial_state: |\psi(0)\rangle = |0\rangle = |0\rangle^{\otimes n}: walker localized at site x = 0 (assumed choice for the tiny instance).

steps.description: Prepare the site register in the localized state |0\rangle (eq_4). Fix N = 4, theta = theta' = pi/2, phi = phi' = 0 so that |\alpha_k\rangle = (|2k\rangle+|2k+1\rangle)/\sqrt{2} and |\beta_k\rangle = (|2k+1\rangle+|2k+2 \bmod 4\rangle)/\sqrt{2} (eq_2).

Apply the tessellation-0 reflection U_0 = 2\sum_k|\alpha_k\rangle\langle\alpha_k| - I, which acts as the same 2x2 unitary on each pair {2k,2k+1} (eq_3; in the relabeled picture this is I \otimes C_0, eq_7).

Apply the tessellation-1 reflection U_1 = 2\sum_k|\beta_k\rangle\langle\beta_k| - I, acting on the shifted pairs {2k+1, 2k+2 mod N} (eq_3). Steps 2-3 together implement one application of U = U_1 U_0.
Repeat steps 2-3 a total of t times to realize |\psi(t)\rangle = U^t|\psi(0)\rangle (eq_4).
Measure the site register in the computational basis to sample x with probability p_t(x) (eq_4); repeat the whole circuit for each t in 0,...,T-1 and for enough shots to estimate p_t.

specification.measurement: Projective measurement of all n site qubits in the computational basis; outcome bitstring decoded as integer x gives one sample from p_t(x) = |\langle x|U^t|0\rangle|^2.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate p_t(x) from shot frequencies for each t < T; form the Cesaro average \bar{p}_T(x) (eq_5); compare with the limiting distribution \pi(x), which for the tiny instance is computed classically by diagonalizing the 4x4 matrix U and applying eq_5; compute the total-variation distance and the mixing time M_\varepsilon (eq_6).
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied, so a single minimal construction was chosen: a two-tessellation coinless walk on a cycle with two-site polygons, instance N = 4, theta = theta' = pi/2, phi = phi' = 0, initial state |0\rangle.
N is even so that both nearest-neighbour tessellations tile the cycle exactly.
Each tessellation operator is a reflection 2P - I about the span of its polygon states (standard staggered-walk form); the paper's 'specific family of evolution operators' may be more general.
Polygon parameters are uniform across each tessellation (translation invariance).
The coined-equivalence is modelled only as the parity relabeling of eq_7; the paper's 'extended coined' operator factorization is not reconstructed.
Mixing time is defined with respect to the time-averaged distribution in total-variation distance.
missing_information: The specific family of coinless evolution operators studied in the paper (parametrization, number and shape of tessellations).
The explicit form of the 'extended coined' walk (coin dimension, shift operator, extra coin or conditional operations) and the general-form equivalence argument between coinless and coined walks.
The asymptotic features of the 1D walk (spreading rate, limiting velocity distribution) and the example tessellations considered.
Analytic expressions or numerical results for the mixing time and limiting distributions on cycles (dependence on N, parity of N, and initial state).
Whether the paper analyzes instantaneous or time-averaged mixing, and which distance measure it uses.
